rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: True knowledge begins by grasping causes, and inquiry begins by seeking the cause behind what is observed.
rows.anchor: hakīkat-i ilmin başı idrâk-i illet ve taharriyât-ı ilmiyenin başı da taharrî-i illettir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A well-defined question is half of knowledge: first identify what one seeks, then frame the question clearly.
rows.anchor: Fi’l-vâki‘tasvîr-i suâl, yani vaz‘-ı mes’ele ilmin nısfıdır denilir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commanded question and answer are divine inspiration and inner signs, showing that God governs the human inner life.
rows.anchor: O “bunu sor” ve arkasından da “şu cevâbı ver” diye emrediyor; bu suretle bunlarda Allah’a delâlet eden âyât-ı enfüsiye oluyorlar.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Observing changes in the heavens and earth makes their need for an owner and administrator felt, so the answer that they belong to God is self-evident.
rows.anchor: semâvât u arzın tehavvülât ve teessürâtını görmek ve bunların bir mâlik-i müdebbire muhtaç olduğunu hissetmek Allah’ın varlığını duymak demektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since God is the universal cause, creator, owner, and ruler, answering “to God” is an analytically self-evident proposition.
rows.anchor: Ve zaten Allah demek bunların illet-i küllü, hâlıkı, mâliki, hâkimi demektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heavens and earth point to spatial beings and events, while the following verse points to temporal beings and events; together they establish God's mastery of both space and time and the core of proofs for the Creator and resurrection.
rows.anchor: sonra وَلَهُۥ مَا سَكَنَ فِى ٱلَّيْلِ وَٱلنَّهَارِ âyetiyle zaman ve hâdisât-ı zamâniye irâe olunarak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sura's opening statements about creating the heavens and earth and making darkness and light summarize spatial and temporal perspectives; creation and ordering signal causality, which these verses unfold.
rows.anchor: sûrenin evvelindeki خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضَ وَجَعَلَ ٱلظُّلُمَٰتِ وَٱلنُّورَ fıkraları da mekânî ve zamânî bu iki nokta-i nazarı icmâl etmiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After identifying God as the cause of things, reflection should infer and witness His essential and moral attributes through successive questions and answers, moving from the beginning toward resurrection over time.
rows.anchor: Allah teâlâ’nın sıfât-ı zâtiye ve mâneviyesini istidlâl ve istişhad ederek anlamaya

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although God owns all creation and could act as He wills without any superior cause or standard, He voluntarily committed Himself to mercy as grace and made it His character.
rows.anchor: bizzat kendisi tefaddul[^3] ve ihsan tarîkiyle bütün milkine rahmeti iltizam edip kendi Zât-ı mukaddesine bi’l-ihtiyar vâcib kıldı, rahmeti ahlâk edindi.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In God's relation to creation and lordship, mercy is His primary and expected influence; wrath is secondary, arising from created beings' mutual wrongdoing and distance from divine morality.
rows.anchor: Allah tarafından evvelen ve bizzat gelen ve muntazar olan hükm ü te’sîr rahmetten ibarettir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even secondary wrath serves mercy: pain is not intended for itself but distinguishes and preserves pleasure and leads from fleeting delights to lasting ones.
rows.anchor: Elemin halkı maksûdun li-zâtihi değil, lezzete ta‘ayyün vermek, onun hükmünü muhafaza etmek ve lezâiz-i fâniyeden lezâiz-i bâkıyeye geçmek içindir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By mercy, God initially created people with sound nature, reason, choice, and freedom, guided them to knowledge and unity through signs, messengers, and books, and invited them to mercy while warning them against punishment.
rows.anchor: insanları da ibtidâen fıtrat-ı selîme üzere halk etmiş, akl ü ihtiyar ve hürriyet vermiş ve enfüs ü âfâkta nasb-ı âyât ve irsâl-i rusül ve inzâl-i kütüb ile marifet ve tevhîdine hidâyet eylemiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because He prescribed mercy, God does not hasten punishment for those who misuse freedom, reject signs and books, deny and mock messengers, and adopt conduct opposed to divine morality; He accepts repentance, or they would already have perished with earlier peoples.
rows.anchor: ukūbeti ta‘cil etmez, tevbe ve ilticâyı kabul eder, yoksa sizi de çoktan o mahv u münkariz olanların yanına gönderirdi.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Merciful respite cannot continue forever: it has an appointed term, after which God will answer defiant acts with wrath and sustain the order of mercy forever.
rows.anchor: bu imhâl, nâmütenâhî gidemez, elbette bunun bir ecel-i müsemmâsı vardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will gather the deniers, together with earlier deniers, in graves and at the gathering place; He will grant eternal mercy to those who follow His approval and punish the others for polytheism and sin.
rows.anchor: kabirlerde ve mahşer yerinde- toplayacak da rızâsına doğru gidenleri rahmet-i ebediyesiyle bekâm ederken sizin de şirk ü mâsiyetlerinizin cezâsını verecektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is no doubt either about this gathering or about the coming of the Day of Resurrection.
rows.anchor: Bunda, bu cem‘de ve bu kıyamet gününün geleceğinde hiç şekk ü şüphe yoktur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who lose themselves waste their original nature, sound reason, and special capacity through misuse; they then disbelieve the truth and wrong themselves.
rows.anchor: Nefislerini ziyan edenler, yani kendilerinin rahmet-i ilâhiyeden sermayeleri olan fıtrat-ı asliyeyi, akl-ı selîmi, isti‘dâd-ı mahsûsu sû’-i isti‘mâl ile zâyi‘edenlerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Present appearances can reverse with time: what seems sweet today may be bitter tomorrow, and today's pain may become tomorrow's sweetness.
rows.anchor: Bugün tatlı görünenler yarın acı, bugün acı gelenler[^5] yarın tatlı olabilir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everything dwelling by night or day, in darkness or daylight, hidden or open, still or moving, belongs to God.
rows.anchor: gece ile gündüzde sâkin olan, gecelerin zulmeti ve gündüzlerin ziyâsı içinde mesken tutan, gizli açık, sâkin ve müteharrik her şey de O’nundur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God hears all that can be heard and knows everything completely; no word or deed remains hidden from Him.
rows.anchor: Bütün mesmû‘âtı tamamıyla işitir ve her şeyi tamamıyla bilir. O’ndan gizli kalacak ne bir kavl vardır, ne de bir fiil.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because mercy precedes wrath, people must not infer that later wrath will never come or that misuse of the self carries no responsibility; they should believe in the afterlife and prepare for it.
rows.anchor: bidâyeten gazab gelmiyor diye nihâyeten de gelmez, nefislerin sû’-i isti‘mâlinin hiç mes’ûliyeti olmaz zannedip de nefislere ziyan etmemeli, âhirete inanmalı ve o gün için çalışmalıdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question rejects taking anyone besides God as protector, refuge, or object of worship, since He is the creator of the heavens and earth.
rows.anchor: Gökleri ve yeri yaratan, bütün fıtratları yapan Allah’tan başkasına mı gönül verip velâyetine sığınacağım, mâbud tanıyacağım?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God provides sustenance but is not fed and is free of every need; worshiping needy beings that depend on others is irrational and disgraceful.
rows.anchor: Böyle ganî li-zâtihi ve muhsin li-zâtihi olan yaratanı bırakıp da, zâtında muhtaç olanlara, gayrıdan intifâ‘ihtiyacında bulunanlara perestiş etmek aklen bile ne kadar büyük şenâ‘at ve hamâkat olduğu da âşikârdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fâtır is an active participle from fatr, while fitrat is its type-form or verbal noun.
rows.anchor: “Fâtır”, “fatr”dan ism-i fâ‘ildir ki, “fıtrat” bunun binâ’-i nev‘i veya hâsıl-ı masdarıdır.

rows.speaker: İbn Abbas
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says he did not know the meaning of fâtır until two Bedouins disputed over a well and one said he had begun digging it.
rows.anchor: İbn Abbas’tan mervîdir ki “Ben” demiş, “‘fâtır’ın mânasını iyice bilmiyordum, nihâyet bana iki a‘râbî bir kuyu hakkında muhakemeye geldiler.

rows.speaker: İbn Enbârî
rows.claim: Ibn Enbârî explains that fatr originally means splitting or opening something at its beginning.
rows.anchor: İbn Enbârî de şöyle beyan etmiştir ki: “Fatr”ın aslı bir şeyi ibtidâsında şakketmek, yarmaktır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Turkish word yaratmak is especially connected with the sense of opening or splitting that grounds the term fatr.
rows.anchor: Bundan anlaşılır ki lisânımızdaki “yaratmak” kelimesi daha ziyade bununla alâkadardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before contingent beings exist, they are indistinct nonexistence; absolute space likewise appears closed and unbroken, an analogy for nonexistence.
rows.anchor: hepsi zulmette, ‘ademde, bitişik, kapanık, retk bir hâlde bulunur ki insanlara ‘adem-i mutlak ancak bu suretle tavazzuh edebilir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emergence of a light or star at a point can be pictured as splitting space open like a hole or window; the first existence of contingent beings is such a rupture, called fatr, with its initial state called fitrat.
rows.anchor: Ve işte mevcûdât-ı hâdisenin ilk ân-ı vücûdu fezâ-yı ‘ademin böyle bir yarılışıdır. Bu şak, bu yarış “fatr”, ve bu ilk yarılıştaki hâl-i vücûd bir “fıtrat”tır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an describes the heavens and earth as once joined and then split; this is cited as an example of the rupture imagery.
rows.anchor: Nitekim أَنَّ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضَ كَانَتَا رَتْقًۭا فَفَتَقْنَٰهُمَا [el-Enbiyâ 21/30][^10] gelecektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fitrat includes prior knowledge and determination and is a component of khalq; khalq and hilqat, like fatr and fitrat, are also used synonymously.
rows.anchor: Binâen‘aleyh fıtrat, bir ilm-i mütekaddim[^11] ile takdir etmek mânasını da mutazammın olan “halk” mefhûmunun cüz’-i sânîsi demektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creation from nothing and creation from an original material both begin with a split, as one substance or being emerges from another.
rows.anchor: ‘Ademden yaratılış böyle olduğu gibi, bir madde-i asliyeden yaratılış da böyledir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A split destroys the prior material but repairs and brings into existence the new being; the first rupture from nothing is wholly good rather than corrupting.
rows.anchor: Bu şak evvelki maddeye nazaran bir harâb ü fesad, fakat ondan çıkan yeni mevcûda nazaran da bir şakk-ı ıslah ve vücuddur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Any first actual origination, with or without prior matter, is fatr, and its initial state is fitrat; recurring continuation of that state is nature, so fitrat precedes nature.
rows.anchor: İşte evvelemirde mekâniyyâtta bâriz olan bu mâna dolayısıyla herhangi bir şeyin madde ile gerek mesbuk olsun ve gerek olmasın bilfiil olan ilk îcâd u ibdâ‘ına “fatr” ve ilk hâlet-i vücûdiyesine “fıtrat” tesmiye olunmuştur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As creator of the heavens and earth, God originates all fitras and supplies their natural needs for continued existence, while remaining free of need and seeking no benefit from creation.
rows.anchor: Allah hem bütün fıtratları yapar yaratır, hem de onların mukadder olan devam ve tevâlîleri için muhtaç oldukları havâic-i tabî‘iyeyi de bahş u ihsan eder.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God asks for submission to His commands so that, in the next stage, He may bring creatures to eternal mercy and protect them from His wrath.
rows.anchor: Ancak hâlet-i sâniyede rahmet-i ebediyesine îsâl ile onları gazabından vikāye için kendine, evâmir ü ahkâmına islâm ve inkıyad ister.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad was commanded to be first among those who submit to God sincerely and obey Him, and was firmly forbidden to be among the polytheists.
rows.anchor: bana Müslümanların; Allah’a teslîm-i nefs ile ihlâs üzere inkıyad edenlerin evveli olmam emredildi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet says that if he disobeys his Lord and opposes the commands and prohibitions, he fears punishment on a great day.
rows.anchor: her hâlde büyük bir günün azâbından korkarım.

rows.speaker: Âsım’dan Ebû Bekir Şu‘be; Hamza ve Kisâî
rows.claim: Shu‘ba's transmission from Asim, Hamza, and Kisai read يُصْرَفْ in the known passive form; if punishment is turned away, God has truly shown that person mercy.
rows.anchor: Âsım’dan Ebû Bekir Şu‘be rivayeti, Hamza ve Kisâî kıraati ma‘lum sîgasıyla يُصْرَفْ olduğuna[^12] göre

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being spared punishment is true divine mercy and the manifest victory: clear, certain deliverance and the great object sought.
rows.anchor: Ve işte o fevz-i mübîn; o açık, kat‘î halâs, o aranan büyük murad da budur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhurr includes pain, grief, fear, or a hardship such as illness or poverty that causes one or more of them.
rows.anchor: bir elem, bir hüzün, bir korku veya bunların birine veya hepsine bâ‘is olacak hastalık, fakirlik veya sâire gibi bir sıkıntı, bir tazyik dokundurursa

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kh ayr means removing distress or granting pleasure, joy, or benefits such as health, wealth, and victory.
rows.anchor: durru def‘eder veya lezzet, sürur veya bunların birine

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only God can remove a hardship, and He can grant every good; because He can do all things, He can also preserve or remove a benefit.
rows.anchor: Binâen‘aleyh onu idâme ve izâleye de kādirdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is sovereign over His servants, always superior and victorious; no one can oppose His harm or contest His good.
rows.anchor: her vechile üstün, dâima gālib ve kāhir bir kādirdir. Ne durruna mu‘âraza edilebilir, ne hayrına müzâhame.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God acts wisely and knows His servants' conditions completely; He alone is wise and knowing, the source of every sign of wisdom and good.
rows.anchor: Ve O ef‘âlinde hakîm, ibâdının ahvâline Habîr ü Alîm’dir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Given God's power, sovereignty, wisdom, and knowledge, no other can be worshiped as an independent or shared deity.
rows.anchor: böyle kâşif-i durr, mu‘tî-i hayr, Kādir ü Kāhir, Hakîm ü Habîr bir Allah’ın karşısına başkası nasıl velî ittihaz edilir de istiklâlen veya iştirâken mâbud tanınabilir?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing names Hakim and Habir, with their wisdom and goodness, introduce a proof of Muhammad's prophethood through testimony to truth and the basis of certainty, which the author calls a central principle of wisdom.
rows.anchor: Bu Hakîm ü Habîr fâsılası ve bu hikmet ü hayr noktasında ilm-i hikmetin en mühim esasını teşkil eden şâhid-i hak ve menât-ı yakīn meselesi ile nübüvvet-i Muhammediyeyi takrir siyâkında buyuruluyor ki:
